summary: @picsart/gen-ai preinstall executes heavily obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun runtime
details: The package's `scripts.preinstall` runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub when not already present and then invokes Bun to execute the sibling file `math_init.js` at install time. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated blob using a rotating string-array (`WV8StW`) and a custom-alphabet decoder (`hc1jfK9`) over an opaque literal, with hex-named identifiers throughout; no plaintext endpoints, purpose strings, or references relating to the package's advertised generative-AI CLI are visible. Delivery through an alternate runtime (Bun) executed on `npm install` routes the payload around Node-based install-time inspection, and the depth of obfuscation is consistent with hiding network destinations and behavior. The @picsart scope is a known target of recent npm supply-chain compromises; the combination of alt-runtime delivery, opaque payload, and misleading filename (`math_init.js`) inside a gen-ai package is not consistent with legitimate install-time work.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
